definition: Parallel play is a social play pattern in which children play alongside other children without much direct interaction or shared activity. In the source, it is described as one of the play styles children showed more often in a community playground, apparently when fewer familiar play partners were available.

reasons: The packet supports that children showed more parallel play on the community playground and that this appears related to available/familiar play partners, but it does not define parallel play as children playing alongside others without direct interaction or shared activity.
The definition adds an explanatory generalization about the play pattern itself that is not stated in the supplied source.

The definition’s description of parallel play as “children play alongside other children without much direct interaction or shared activity” is not explicitly supported by the provided packet text (the packet mentions parallel play levels by setting but does not define what parallel play involves).

The claim that it was “apparently when fewer familiar play partners were available” is not stated in those exact terms; the packet only says the difference “appears to be a function of available play partners” and that children “are not comfortable playing with children they do not know,” which does not fully substantiate the “fewer familiar play partners” phrasing.
